titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Entry into Jerusalem in Glory (ch. 107)
part: ch. 107 — the entry into Jerusalem in glory
about: The chapter heading names Christ's entry into Jerusalem in glory, and the text answers with a chain of prophecies in the frame "and as X prophesied and said": Isaiah, Zechariah, David, Solomon and Ezra, then Jacob's blessing of Judah (the son of a lion, the lordship that does not depart). The author then explains that "Beloved", "Messiah" and "Jesus" all name Christ, cites the Ascension of Isaiah and the psalms of the unicorn's horn, and ends with Habakkuk's "horns in his hands" read as the nails of the cross.

sentences.i: Chapter 107: Concerning the entry into Jerusalem in glory
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በአቱ is በአት 'entry, entering' (from ቦአ 'enter') + -ሁ 'his': the ending is the suffix -ቱ, not the construct ending -ተ, so literally 'his entry, Jerusalem', the suffix anticipating the place, and the sense is 'the entry into Jerusalem' (?). The reference is Christ's entry into Jerusalem, as the prophecies below make clear. በስብሐት is በ- 'in' + ስብሐት 'glory, praise'.

sentences.l: And-concerning entry-of Jerusalem in-glory prophesied prophets while he-says Isaiah prophet: 'Shine-you(f), shine-you(f), Jerusalem; has-arrived light-your(f), and-glory-of God has-risen over-you(f).' And-as prophesied Zechariah prophet and-said: 'Rejoice-you(f), rejoice-you(f), daughter-of Zion, and-let-exult(?) Jerusalem in-joy.' And-as prophesied David and-said: 'From-mouth-of children and-infants you-prepared(?) praise on-account-of enemy, that you-bring-down(?)-him the-enemy and-the-oppressor.' And-as prophesied Solomon and-said: 'Children-your taught in-the-presence-of God, and-will-rejoice nations within-you(f).' And-as prophesied David father-his and-said: 'Blow-you(pl) horn in-Zion on-day-of rising, on-marked day feast-our, for ordinance-his for-Israel it.' And-as prophesied Ezra scribe and-said: 'Go-out-you(pl), make-you(pl) feast in-gladness, and-say(pl)-to-her to-daughter-of Zion: Rejoice-you(f), behold king-your(f) has-arrived.' And-as prophesied Isaiah prophet and-said: 'Rejoice-you(f) Jerusalem, rejoice-you(f), behold king-your(f) has-arrived, while he-rides upon ass, he-whose-reward with-him and-work-his before face-his.' And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Blessed he-who comes in-name-of God.'
sentences.i: And concerning the entry into Jerusalem in glory the prophets prophesied, Isaiah the prophet saying: 'Shine, shine, Jerusalem! Your light has come, and the glory of God has risen over you.' And as Zechariah the prophet prophesied and said: 'Rejoice, rejoice, daughter of Zion, and let Jerusalem exult in joy.' And as David prophesied and said: 'Out of the mouth of children and infants you have prepared praise, because of the enemy, that you may bring down the enemy and the oppressor.' And as Solomon prophesied and said: 'Your children are taught in the presence of God, and the nations will rejoice within you.' And as his father David prophesied and said: 'Blow the horn in Zion on the day of the rising (?), on the appointed day of our feast, for it is his ordinance for Israel.' And as Ezra the scribe prophesied and said: 'Go out, make a feast with gladness, and say to the daughter of Zion: Rejoice! Behold, your king has come.' And as Isaiah the prophet prophesied and said: 'Rejoice, Jerusalem, rejoice! Behold, your king has come, riding on an ass, he whose reward is with him and whose work is before his face.' And as David the prophet prophesied and said: 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of God.'
sentences.n: This long unit has no ፤ or ። inside it, so it is kept whole as cut by script. It opens a catena of prophecy for Christ's entry into Jerusalem (the Palm Sunday scene), strung on the frame ወበከመ ተነበየ X ወይቤ 'and as X prophesied and said' (ወ- 'and', በ- + ከመ 'as'; perfect ተነበየ, tä-stem of n-b-y). The quotations and their sources: Isaiah 60:1 ('Shine, Jerusalem, your light has come'; አብርሂ is the feminine imperative, -ኪ the feminine 'your'); Zechariah 9:9 ('Rejoice, daughter of Zion'); Psalm 8:2 (the mouths of children and infants, quoted in Matthew 21:16 at this very entry); ምሁራን 'taught, trained' recalls Isaiah 54:13 (children taught by God), which the text gives to Solomon, and the 'nations rejoicing in you' is a different verse again, so this is a loose citation; Psalm 81:3 (80:4 in the Septuagint), the horn blown on the feast, given to 'David his father'; Ezra the scribe is credited with a saying that echoes Nehemiah 8 and Zechariah 9:9, not a verse I can match (?); then Isaiah again with the king on an ass (Zechariah 9:9, with 'his reward is with him and his work before him' from Isaiah 40:10 / 62:11); and Psalm 118:26 (117:26), 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord', which the crowds cry in Matthew 21:9. Source slip kept as printed: ን ፡ ጉሥኪ is one word, ንጉሥኪ 'your king', split by a stray wordspace (ንጉሥኪ is spelled whole earlier in this unit). Uncertain: ሠርቅ 'rising' (sunrise, new moon?) in 'day of the rising' (?); እምርት is 'sign, mark', so 'marked/appointed day'; ወበልዋ is ወ- + the 2mp imperative በሉ + the suffix -ዋ 'to her' (compare በልዎሙ in ch. 106c), 'and say to her', continuing the plural ፃኡ ግበሩ. Further forms to watch: ወየብቢ — I cannot identify the root; 'exult, cry out' is guessed from Zechariah 9:9, and a 2fs imperative would not normally carry የ- (?). አስተዳሎከ is either 'you prepared' (2ms perfect, contracted) or 'he prepared for you' (3ms + -ከ) (?); the Psalm's sense favours the first. ትንሥቶ is a 2ms subjunctive + -ኦ 'him' (doubled by ለጸላኢ); 'bring down' is guessed from the sense, the root being uncertain (?). ወለገፋዒ: ገፋዒ is the agent noun of ገፍዐ 'push, oppress', so 'oppressor' (?). ሥርዐቱ is ሥርዐት 'ordinance' + -ሁ 'his'. በኀበ is 'before, in the presence of'. ዘዕሴቱ 'he whose reward' is ዘ- 'who/whose' + ዕሴት 'reward' + -ሁ.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ሰብሑከ ፡ አኀዊከ ፡ እደዊከ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ዘባኖሙ ፡ ለጸላእትከ ፡ ወይሰግዲ ፡ ለከ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ እምከ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Jacob son-of Isaac and-said: 'Judah, they-praised-you brothers-your; hands-your upon backs-their of-enemies-your; and-they-will-bow to-you children-of mother-your;
sentences.i: And as Jacob the son of Isaac prophesied, he said: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you; your hands are on the backs of your enemies; and the sons of your mother will bow down to you;
sentences.n: Genesis 49:8, Jacob's blessing of Judah, here read as a prophecy of Christ from Judah's line. ሰብሑከ is the 3mp perfect ሰብሑ 'they praised' with the suffix -ከ 'you'; ዘባኖሙ 'their backs' is ዘባን 'back' (as in the published parts) + -ሙ, and ለጸላእትከ is 'of your enemies' with the ለ- of possession. ወይሰግዲ is printed with the ending -ዲ, not the usual plural -ዱ; I read it as 'they will bow' (?), with ደቂቀ 'sons of' (the construct, identical in form with the accusative) before እምከ as its subject, so the parse is uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወኢየሐጽጽ ፡ ምልክና ፡ እምይሁዳ ፡ ወምስፍና ፡ እምአባሉ ፡ እስከ ፡ አመ ፡ ይረክብ ፡ ዘጽኑሕ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወውእቱ ፡ ተስፋሆሙ ፡ ለአሕዛብ ።
sentences.l: and-not will-fail lordship from-Judah, and-rule from-limbs-his, until when he-finds that-which-firm for-him; and-he hope-their for-nations.
sentences.i: and lordship will not fail from Judah, nor rule from his limbs (?), until he finds what is fixed for him (?); and he is the hope of the nations.
sentences.n: Genesis 49:10, the lordship that does not leave Judah. ምልክና 'lordship, dominion' (the published ch. 43 has ምልክናሁ) and ምስፍና 'rule, governorship' are both abstract nouns in -ና, and here neither carries a suffix, so not 'your lordship'. አባል is 'limb, member' (as in the published parts); the Hebrew has 'from between his feet', so 'limbs' here probably means the body from which descendants come (?). ይረክብ ዘጽኑሕ ሎቱ is literally 'he finds that which is firm for him': ጽኑሕ is 'firm, abiding' (as in ch. 2–8), so 'what is fixed for him'; whose it is and what it is remain uncertain (?). The last clause, 'and he is the hope of the nations', is the Christian reading of the verse.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ጸዐዳ ፡ ስነኒሁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘበረድ ፡ ወፍሡሓት ፡ አዕይንቲሁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወይን ፡ ወየኀፅብ ፡ በወይን ፡ ልብሶ ፡ ወበደመ ፡ አስካል ፡ ሶንዶኖ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወልደ ፡ አንበሳ ፡ ሰከብከ ፡ ወኖምከ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘያነቅሆ ፡ አላ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይረክብ ፡ ዘነዐወ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-prophesied and-said: 'White teeth-his like that-of hail(?), and-glad eyes-his like wine, and-he-washes in-wine garment-his, and-in-blood-of cluster robe-his.' And-again he-prophesied while he-says: 'Judah son-of lion, you-lay-down and-you-slept; there-is-not who-wakes-him except himself, until he-finds the-one-who prevailed(?);
sentences.i: And again he prophesied and said: 'His teeth are white like hail (?), and his eyes are glad like wine, and he washes his garment in wine, and his robe in the blood of the grape-cluster.' And again he prophesied, saying: 'Judah, son of a lion, you lay down and slept; there is no one who wakes him but himself, until he finds the one who prevailed (?);
sentences.n: Genesis 49:12 and 49:9. The two ወካዕበ ተነበየ 'and again he prophesied' (ካዕበ 'again, a second time') mark that the same patriarch is quoted a second and third time. በረድ is 'hail, ice' (the Hebrew and Greek have 'milk' for the teeth), so 'white like hail' (?). ፍሡሓት 'glad, bright' is a feminine plural adjective on አዕይንት 'eyes'. ሶንዶኖ is the Greek loanword σινδών 'linen cloth, robe' with the suffix -ኦ; አስካል is 'cluster of grapes'. In the second quotation ሰከብከ ወኖምከ is 'you lay down and slept' (Genesis 49:9); ዘያነቅሆ 'who wakes him' is ዘ- + ያነቅሆ (ʾa-stem of n-q-h 'be awake'). ዘነዐወ is, I think, 'he who prevailed' (ነዐወ 'conquer', the verb of the Lion of Judah in Revelation 5:5), but this is uncertain (?). እስከ ይረክብ ዘነዐወ repeats the previous unit's ይረክብ ዘ-: I take the ዘ-clause as what he finds; the other possibility, 'until he who prevailed attains (it)', has the ዘ-clause as subject (?).

sentences.t: እምሕዛእትከ ፡ ዕርግ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ባረኮ ፡ ለይሁዳ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ህሎ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ዘይወፅእ ፡ እምኔከ ፡ ዘየኀፅብ ፡ በወይን ፡ ልብሶ ፡ ወክቡር ፡ ምዕራፊሁ ፡ ለፍቁር ፤
sentences.l: from-shoot(?)-your go-up(?). And-again he-blessed-him Judah, his-son, Jacob, and-said-to-him: 'There-is king who goes-out from-you, who washes in-wine garment-his, and-honoured resting-place(?)-his for-the-Beloved;
sentences.i: 'From your shoot (?) go up.' And again Jacob blessed Judah, his son, and said to him: 'There is a king who comes out of you, who washes his garment in wine; and honoured is his resting-place (?), for the Beloved;
sentences.n: Genesis 49:9–12 continues, Judah the lion's whelp. ሕዛእት (here with the preposition እም- and -ከ) I take as 'shoot, sprout' (?). ዕርግ is the 2ms imperative of ዐርገ 'go up' (or possibly a noun 'ascent'), not a perfect 'you went up' (?). ባረኮ is the perfect ባረከ 'bless' plus -ኦ 'him', doubled by ለይሁዳ; ወልዲ is, in the published parts' spelling, 'his son' (-ዲ for -ሁ), so ያዕቆብ is the subject placed last, 'Jacob blessed Judah, his son'; the other reading, ወልዲ as 'son of' ('Judah son of Jacob', with the blesser unnamed), is possible (?). ወይቤሎ is 'and he said to him'. ህሎ ንጉሥ 'there is a king' (ህሎ 'there is/was'). ምዕራፍ is 'resting-place' (from ዐረፈ 'rest'), as in the published parts (?), so 'his resting-place is honoured'. ለፍቁር 'for the Beloved' is a Christian addition to the verse: ፍቁር 'beloved' (from ፈቀረ 'love') is the title the next units explain. The ፤ ends mid-sentence; the explanation of ፍቁር follows.

The first of three glosses. ብሂል is the verbal noun of ብህለ 'say', used as a gloss-marker: 'saying' = 'that is to say, it means'. So: 'Beloved' stands for 'Christ'. ክርስቶስ is the Greek-derived 'Christ', anointed. The sequence of ብሂል clauses is a teacher's equation of the three names; flag the pattern once, it recurs in the next unit.

sentences.t: ወመሲሕ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ወኢየሱስ ፡ ብሂል ፡ መድኀኔ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: and-Messiah saying Christ saying, and-Jesus saying saviour-of people saying;
sentences.i: and 'Messiah' means 'Christ', and 'Jesus' means 'Saviour of the people';
sentences.n: Same ብሂል gloss formula. መሲሕ (Hebrew mashiach 'anointed') is equated with ክርስቶስ (Greek christos 'anointed'); ኢየሱስ 'Jesus' is explained as መድኀኔ ሕዝብ 'saviour-of people' (construct chain; መድኀኒ 'saviour' from ድኅነ 'be saved'). The explanation of Jesus as 'Saviour' echoes Matthew 1:21.

sentences.t: ወነቢያትሰ ፡ ይሰምይዎ ፡ በሥውር ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ወይብልዎ ፡ ፍቁር ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዕርገቱ ፡ በትንቢት ፡ ውእተ ፡ አሚረ ፡ ይወርድ ፡ ፍቁር ፡ እምሰማይ ፡ ወየኀሪ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ፲ወ፪ ፡ ሐዋርያት ፤
sentences.l: And-the-prophets-indeed they-name-him in-secret to-Christ, and-they-call-him Beloved. And-said Isaiah at ascension-his in-prophecy: 'That day will-descend the-Beloved from-heaven and-will-choose for-him twelve apostles;
sentences.i: The prophets, for their part, name Christ in secret and call him 'the Beloved'. And Isaiah said, in a prophecy about his ascension: 'On that day the Beloved will come down from heaven and choose for himself twelve apostles;
sentences.n: The enclitic -ሰ in ወነቢያትሰ marks contrast ('the prophets, for their part, ...'). ይሰምይዎ and ይብልዎ are 3mp imperfects with the suffix -ዎ 'him' (ሰመየ 'name', ብህለ 'say'; ይብልዎ ፍቁር 'they say of him, Beloved', i.e. call him). በሥውር 'in secret' (ሥውር 'hidden'). ኀበ ዕርገቱ 'at his ascension' (ኀበ 'at, where'; 'in the matter of' is the sense I give it in the English) (?). The quotation is not in the canonical Isaiah but in the Ascension of Isaiah (3:13–18, the descent of the Beloved from the seventh heaven and his choosing of twelve apostles), a work preserved whole in Geʿez. ወየኀሪ ሎቱ is 'and he will choose for himself' (ኀረየ 'choose'); ፲ወ፪ is the numeral 12, 'twelve'; ሐዋርያት 'apostles'.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ርኢኩ ፡ ዕርገቶ ፡ ለፍቁር ፡ ወልድ ፡ እስከ ፡ ሳብዕ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ይትቄበልዎ ፡ መላእክት ፡ ወሊቃነ ፡ መላእክት ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይትሌዐል ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ እምኔሆሙ ።
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'I-saw ascension-his of-the-Beloved Son up-to seventh heaven, and-while they-receive-him angels and-chiefs-of angels, while he-is-lifted-up exceedingly above-them.'
sentences.i: And again he said: 'I saw the ascension of the Beloved Son up to the seventh heaven; and while angels and archangels were receiving him, he was raised up far above them.'
sentences.n: Again the Ascension of Isaiah (chapters 9–11), the prophet's vision of the Beloved's ascent through the heavens to the seventh. ሊቃነ መላእክት 'chiefs-of angels' = archangels (ሊቅ 'chief', construct plural ሊቃነ). ይትቄበልዎ is the imperfect of ተቀበለ 'receive, welcome' (a tä-stem verb that is not passive) + -ዎ 'him'; ይትሌዐል is 'he is lifted up, rises' (?), the tä-stem ተለዐለ (root l-ʿ-l) of the published parts. ፈድፋደ is the accusative adverb 'exceedingly'.

sentences.t: ወዳዊትኒ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ወፍቁርሰ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወልድ ፡ ዘ፩ቀርኑ ፤
sentences.i: And David too said: 'And the Beloved, for his part, is like the son of the one-horned beast;
sentences.n: Psalm 29:6 (28:6 in the Septuagint): 'the beloved like a son of unicorns'. ዘ፩ቀርኑ is ዘ- 'who' + the numeral 1 + ቀርኑ 'his horn', 'the one who has one horn', the unicorn of older English (Greek monokerōs), here 'the one-horned beast'. The numeral stands inside the word as printed. -ኒ 'too' and -ሰ 'indeed' are enclitics. Note the psalmist's 'beloved' is read as Christ, as just explained.

sentences.i: And again he said: 'And from the horns of the one-horned beast — my solitary self (?);
sentences.n: Psalm 22:21 (21:22 in the Septuagint), the end of the verse about being saved from the horns of the unicorn; the text gives only these closing words, and the verb of saving is not in this unit. ለብሕቱትየ is ለ- marking the object (as in the published parts) + ብሕቱት + -የ 'my'; ብሕቱት is from ብሕት 'alone, solitary', so 'my solitary one, my lone self' (?). I do not give 'humility': the form says solitude.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ወይትሌዐል ፡ ቀርንየ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘ፩ቀርኑ ፡ አቅርንትሰ ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ መንግሥታተ ፡ ዓለም ፡ ወዘይትበህልሂ ፡ ዘ፩ቀርኑ ፡ ለመንግሥቱ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይትቃረኖ ፡ እስመ ፡ መላኬ ፡ ነገሥት ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ ይስዕር ፡ ወለዘፈቀደ ፡ ይሠይም ፡ በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወእምክቡዳነ ፡ አቅርንት ፡ ዘእምኔሆሙ ፡ ኣስተፈሥሐከ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'And-it-will-be-exalted horn-my like that-of the-one-horned.' The-horns-indeed are-interpreted kingdoms-of world, and-that-which-is-said-also 'of-the-one-horned' as-for-kingdom-his there-is-not who opposes-him; for ruler-of kings he, to-him who wished he-overthrows, and-to-him-who-wished he-appoints; as said David: 'And-from-heavy(?) horns, that-from-them he-made-glad-you;
sentences.i: And again he said: 'And my horn will be exalted like that of the one-horned beast.' The horns, now, are interpreted as the kingdoms of the world; and as for what is called 'the one-horned one's', there is no one who opposes him in his kingdom, for he is the ruler of kings: whomever he wishes he overthrows, and whomever he wishes he sets up. As David said: 'And from the heavy (?) horns, from them he made you glad (?);
sentences.n: Psalm 92:10 (91:11 in the Septuagint), 'my horn shall be exalted like the unicorn's'. Here the author stops to interpret the symbol: አቅርንት 'horns' stand for መንግሥታተ ዓለም 'kingdoms of the world' (ይተረጐም 'is interpreted', tä-stem of ተርጐመ 'translate, interpret'), while the lone horn of the unicorn means one unrivalled kingdom. ዘይትበህልሂ is ዘ- + the tä-stem 'what is said' + -ሂ 'also'; ዘይትቃረኖ 'who opposes him' (ተቃረነ 'oppose' (?)). መላኬ ነገሥት 'ruler of kings' (መላኪ 'ruler', construct). ይስዕር 'overthrows' (ሰዐረ 'abolish, destroy'; the construction after ፈቀደ is hard) (?) and ይሠይም 'appoints' (ሠየመ). The closing quotation is Psalm 45:8 (44:9 in the Septuagint), the verse of the ivory palaces, whose 'ivory' (horn, tusk) lets it speak of horns. ክቡዳነ is the accusative plural of ክቡድ 'heavy, weighty', not of ክቡር 'honoured' (whose plural is ክቡራን, used in the next unit); I keep 'heavy (?)', though the author's comment reads it as 'honoured'. ዘእምኔሆሙ is 'that (which is) from them'. ኣስተፈሥሐከ (with the printed variant ኣ for አ) is the ʾastä-stem አስተፈሥሐ 'make glad' (as in the published ወአስተፈሥሒዮሙ) in the 3ms perfect + -ከ 'you', so 'he made you glad'; the plural sense of the Psalm would need አስተፈሥሑከ (?). The ፤ ends the unit mid-sentence; the comment on the quotation follows.

sentences.t: ወዝንቱ ፡ ዘተብህለ ፡ እምክቡራን ፡ ነገሥት ፡ አንተ ፡ ትከብር ፡ ወትትፌሣሕ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ እንባቆም ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ አቅርንት ፡ ውስተ ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወረሰየ ፡ ፍቁረ ፡ በጽንዐ ፡ ኀይሉ ፤
sentences.l: And-this which-was-said from-honoured kings: 'You are-honoured and-you-rejoice,' to-say. And-as prophesied Habakkuk while he-says: 'Horns in hands-his, and-he-set the-Beloved in-firmness-of power-his;
sentences.i: And this is what was said concerning the honoured kings: 'You are honoured and you rejoice' — that is what it says. And as Habakkuk prophesied, saying: 'Horns are in his hands, and he set the Beloved in the firmness of his power;
sentences.n: ዘተብህለ 'which was said' is the passive ተብህለ. The quotation 'you are honoured and rejoice' is the sense of the Psalm 45:8 line just given, read as addressed to the honoured kings; the ብሂል at the end is the same 'that is to say' marker. The next is Habakkuk 3:4, 'horns (rays) in his hands'; where the Greek tradition has 'love', the Geʿez has ፍቁረ, the accusative 'the Beloved' (ረሰየ 'set, make'). In the Hebrew the 'horns' are rays of light; the text takes them as symbols again. በጽንዐ ኀይሉ 'in the firmness of his power' (construct chain: ጽንዕ 'firmness', ኀይል 'power').

sentences.t: ወዘንተኒ ፡ ብሂል ፡ አኃዜ ፡ ስልጣነ ፡ ነገሥ ፡ ት ፡ በቅንዋት ፡ ተቀነወ ፡ እራኁ ፡ ዘሕይወተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ውስቴቶን ፡ እኁዝ ፡ ዘገብረ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ በጽንዐ ፡ ኀይሉ ፡ ፍቁር ፡ ብሂል ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-this-also saying: holder-of authority-of kings with-nails was-nailed, ʾərāḫu(?) he-who life-of all within-them held, that-which did Christ in-firmness-of power-his, the-Beloved, saying.
sentences.i: And this too it says: the holder of the authority of kings was nailed with nails, his ... (?), he who has the life of all, held fast within them (?); what Christ did in the firmness of his power is 'the Beloved' (?).
sentences.n: A hard final unit; the sense is the Christian reading of Habakkuk's 'horns in his hands': the nails of the cross in the hands of the crucified king. Source slip kept as printed: ነገሥ ፡ ት is one word, ነገሥት 'kings', split by a stray wordspace (so አኃዜ ስልጣነ ነገሥት, construct chain 'holder-of authority-of kings'). በቅንዋት ተቀነወ 'with nails he was nailed' (ቅንዋት 'nails', passive ተቀነወ). እራኁ is not a form I can parse; it may be a corrupt or rare word, left as 'his ... (?)'. ውስቴቶን is 'within them' (3fp), most likely the nails (ቅንዋት): I read ዘሕይወተ ኵሉ ውስቴቶን እኁዝ as 'he who has the life of all, held fast in them' (?); እኁዝ 'held, seized'. The final clause I read as 'what Christ did in the strength of his power — that is called the Beloved' (?). The trailing ፨ ፨ ፨ is the edition's closing ornament, kept on this unit.
